name: commit-message-cleanup
goal: The commit-msg hook measures a message file as Git will store it: writtenMessage cleans it as git stripspace does in the strip, whitespace and scissors modes, so whitespace Git never stores is not counted

evidence: Defect, confirmed by Codex and reproduced here: the message 'feat: parity', a blank line, 'alpha' followed by 410 spaces, and 'beta' is refused by the commit-msg hook with 'body has 420 characters; the limit is 400.', while git stripspace leaves 25 bytes of it and Git stores a body of 10 characters. Root cause: writtenMessage in src/utils/commitMessage.ts removed comment lines and what follows the scissors and then trimmed only the two ends of the whole text; in the whitespace mode it trimmed the ends and nothing else. Git cleans every mode but verbatim with strbuf_stripspace: a space, tab, carriage return or newline at the end of each line goes, several blank lines become one, blank lines at the start and the end go, and in the strip mode a line that starts with the comment character goes without leaving a blank line. Contract inspected with real Git 2.37.3 in a temporary repository (oracle.ts and oracle-before.log in commit-cleanup-qa-scripts in the control directory): the hook is given the raw file after an editor, and a file Git has already cleaned of whitespace after -m or -F; commit.cleanup may be strip, whitespace, verbatim, scissors or default, where default is strip after an editor and whitespace without one; the scissors line is the whole line '<comment> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------' and Git cuts there in the scissors mode and whenever the diff is shown with -v, in every mode; core.commentChar moves both the comments and the scissors, and auto chose the hash for a message written in an editor. On the unchanged helper every editor case of that matrix differs from what Git stored. Not at fault and not changed: commitMessage, which measures a stored message and counts a line that starts with a hash; CommitMessageService, which resolves the mode and the comment character; the verbatim mode.

Two test files written before any product change, sha256 in red-test-hashes.txt in commit-cleanup-qa-scripts in the control directory; src/utils/commitMessage.ts identical to f0c387f (product-before.sha256). test/utils/commit-message.test.ts gained four tests of the helper; test/services/commit-message-cleanup.test.ts is new and uses Git as the oracle in a temporary repository whose commit-msg hook is installed by HookInstallService and runs the real command line: git stripspace, with and without --strip-comments and with core.commentChar ';', over 66 texts; real commits written by a scripted editor, with -v, in the scissors and whitespace modes, with another comment character and with -F, each compared character for character with the stored message; refusals of a cleaned message that is still too long or unprefixed, and a --no-verify bypass found by CommitMessageService.stored. Command: bun x vitest run test/utils/commit-message.test.ts test/services/commit-message-cleanup.test.ts. Result: exit 1, 5 failed and 8 passed (RED.log). The faithful failures: the unit test received ['body has 420 characters; the limit is 400.'] for the reported message where [] is required; the real commit written in an editor ended with exit 1 and 'harness: commit refused ... body has 444 characters; the limit is 400.' where Git stores a short body; the helper differs from git stripspace at 'alpha' and its trailing spaces; 61 words between blank lines were refused for 544 characters instead of for their words; the whitespace mode kept the scissors and the diff. The eight that pass on the unchanged helper are the existing six, verbatim as written, and the refusals and the bypass, which must stay as they are.

Repair inside the registered function.commit-message unit and nowhere else: writtenMessage does what Git does to the file. First what stands above the scissors is kept, where the scissors are exactly the line Git writes, at the start of the text or of a line and ended by a newline (wt_status_locate_end); then the text is cleaned as strbuf_stripspace cleans it, with comment lines removed only in the strip mode. The scissors apply in the strip, whitespace and scissors modes, because a hook is not told about -v and Git only writes that line when it will cut there. verbatim is returned as before. The options and the exported names do not change, so CommitMessageService, the guide and every caller stay as they are. Guard in normal verification: both test files run in test:unit, which bun run check and harness verify run; the oracle test fails if the helper and the installed Git ever disagree. Fault reintroduction is proven in a throwaway copy, not in the checkout.

Only src/utils/commitMessage.ts changed in the product, inside the registered function.commit-message unit; its exports and the MessageCleanup options are as they were, so CommitMessageService, the hook wrappers and the guide are untouched. writtenMessage now keeps what stands above the scissors (aboveScissors: the whole line '<comment> ------------------------ >8 ------------------------' at the start of the text or of a line, ended by a newline) and cleans it as git stripspace does (strippedSpace: comment lines go in the strip mode only and leave no blank line; a space, tab or carriage return at the end of a line goes; several blank lines are one; none starts or ends the text). The scissors cut in the strip, whitespace and scissors modes. verbatim returns file.trim() as before, and commitMessage, which measures a stored message and counts a line that starts with a hash, is unchanged. Two things changed after the first green, each re-proven with the final files: the line loop became filter, map and two replaces (83 lines to 72, complexity 19 to 12), and the line-end expression got a lookbehind after a run of 200,000 spaces inside a line took 24 s; it takes 10 ms. Guard wired into normal verification without touching package.json: test/utils/commit-message.test.ts and the new test/services/commit-message-cleanup.test.ts both run in test:unit. tsc reports nothing in these files, eslint, prettier and harness audit pass; the helper has 72 lines. Reason recorded through harness explain add for the 4 symbols; harness units index (dry run) lists nothing, so no manifest changed. Budget not self-approved: source-bytes 3528 and complexity 12 against the frozen 2299 and 10.

Final test files, sha256 in red-test-hashes.txt in commit-cleanup-qa-scripts in the control directory: after the first red and green the oracle test was made independent of the user's Git configuration and a linear-time test was added, so the red was run again with exactly these files against the helper of HEAD f0c387f in a throwaway copy: 5 failed and 9 passed (RED.log), the same five as the first red (RED-first.log), with 'body has 420 characters; the limit is 400.' for the reported message and a real commit written in an editor refused with exit 1. GREEN in the checkout with the same files (shasum -c: 2 OK): bun x vitest run test/utils/commit-message.test.ts test/services/commit-message-cleanup.test.ts exits 0, 14 passed (GREEN.log). What passes: the reported message is cleaned to 'feat: parity', a blank line, 'alpha', 'beta' in the strip, whitespace and scissors modes and has no problem; the helper equals git stripspace, with and without --strip-comments and with core.commentChar ';', on 66 texts; real commits through the installed commit-msg hook are accepted when written in an editor, with -v, in the scissors mode, with comment character ';', in the whitespace mode with -v, and with -F with and without stripped comments, and for each the helper applied to the file the hook was given equals the stored message character for character, with no diff in it; the reported message written in an editor is stored with a body of ten characters. Still refused, with no commit made: 401 characters of body after cleaning, by editor and by -F, and a subject without its prefix; the same message made with --no-verify is stored and CommitMessageService.stored names it. verbatim is measured as written. Real Git matrix of 26 mode, editor and -v combinations (oracle.ts): 10 equal before the repair, 25 after (oracle-before.log, oracle-after.log); the one left is verbatim with -v, which was to stay as it is. Normal hook, command line and writing tests: 11 files, 53 passed (FREEZE.log): commit-message unit, cleanup and service, hooks-commit-msg, hooks, hooks-shared-stages, hook-script, hook-install, guides, writing-limits, explain-brevity. The oracle test also passes under a user configuration that sets commit.cleanup, commit.verbose and core.commentChar.

guard-proof.py in commit-cleanup-qa-scripts in the control directory, in a throwaway copy of the checkout under /tmp where only src/utils/commitMessage.ts is replaced; the checkout is only read and the copy is removed. Each run is bun x vitest run of the two guard files, log guard-<name>.log. The helper of HEAD put back: exit 1, 5 failed and 9 passed. Line ends kept: 6 failed. Several blank lines kept: 4 failed. Blank lines at the start and end kept: 8 failed. Every Unicode blank treated as a line end: 2 failed. The line-end expression without its lookbehind: 1 failed, the linear-time test. The scissors not applied in the whitespace mode: 2 failed. Restored to the repaired helper, equal to the checkout: exit 0, 14 passed. The script exits 0 only when every reintroduction fails and the restored run passes; it exited 0.

Codex independently verified the frozen shell source in an isolated writing:1 checkout. Full CI=1 bun run check passed unchanged deadlines:586root tests plus25existing skips,217CLI,27package plus3existing skips,5serial,473reports, pinnedRust native/Wasm, formatting/types/lint/build/registry/audits and installer checks. Log /tmp/harness-cleanup-ci-root-check.log. Earlier full parallel failures are preserved; their unchanged three files passed7/7 and the complete rerun passed. Actual Git cleanup, verbatim, prefix/body limits, staged/tree activation and shared hook compatibility pass. Core/draft source helper and tests match the tested overlay hashes.
